I was walking into a coffee shop I'd never been to before, phone in one hand, already scrolling through my order in the app.
I wasn't really paying attention to anything directly in front of me.
The whole storefront was glass, spotless, freshly cleaned, apparently.
It was completely invisible to me until the exact moment my face made very direct, very unplanned contact with an entire pane of it.
The sound alone was enough to turn every single head in that coffee shop, a solid, embarrassing thud that echoed way louder than felt physically necessary.
For a second, the entire place went quiet.
It was like everyone was collectively deciding whether this was actually a real emergency or just something to laugh about once they were sure I was fine.
I stumbled back half a step, phone still somehow in my hand.
I just stood there for a second, blinking, trying to process what exactly had just happened to my nose and my dignity simultaneously.
A barista rushed over asking if I was okay.
A couple of people near the window were very obviously trying not to laugh, doing that thing where you look away really fast and bite your lip, shoulders shaking slightly.
One older guy at a nearby table didn't even bother hiding it.
He just laughed openly, loud enough that a couple other customers ended up laughing too, mostly at how unbothered he seemed about it.
I said I was fine, which was mostly true, my nose just a little sore, my pride considerably more damaged than any actual part of my face.
I walked in through the actual door, a few feet to the left, moving a lot more carefully this time.
I ordered my coffee, sat down, and tried to act completely normal.
I could still hear a couple of quiet giggles from the corner table that had gotten a front-row seat to the whole thing.
On my way out, I made an exaggerated show of pointing at the door handle before walking through it properly.
That actually got a genuine laugh out of the same table, breaking whatever remaining awkwardness was left.
I still go to that coffee shop regularly now, and every single time, without fail, I glance at that exact pane of glass, half expecting it to still somehow be waiting there for round two.

The staff still recognize me too, and one barista jokes every single time I walk in, asking if I'd like my coffee with or without a side of glass, which honestly never stops being at least a little funny.
